headline: Bangladesh faces slowest growth, highest inflation in South Asia, IMF warns
summary: The International Monetary Fund forecasts Bangladesh's GDP growth to slow to 3.2% and inflation to hit 10.9% this fiscal year, significantly impacting purchasing power and employment.
details: Bangladesh's economy is projected to experience the slowest growth and highest inflation among South Asian nations, according to a recent forecast by the International Monetary Fund (IMF). This outlook highlights significant challenges ahead for the country.

For the current fiscal year, the IMF predicts the country's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth could drop to 3.2%, with an average annual inflation rate of 10.9%. This growth rate would be the lowest in 3.5 decades, and the inflation rate the highest in 1.5 decades.

This economic slowdown is expected to intensify pressure on investment and job creation. High inflation will further erode people's purchasing power, pushing more individuals into poverty and exacerbating existing economic hardships.

The World Bank recently reported that approximately 8 million people have fallen below the poverty line in Bangladesh over the past four years, with an additional 2.1 million becoming poor last fiscal year. Around 62.5 million people are currently at risk of poverty.

The IMF's projections are notably lower than those from the World Bank (3.4%) and the Asian Development Bank (4%) for the current fiscal year. The government, however, has set a more ambitious growth target of 6.5%.

Underlying issues complicating the situation include a weak banking sector, persistent energy crisis, stagnation in private investment, and a deficit in revenue collection. These factors collectively raise concerns about economic recovery and the overall living standards of the population.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury, while attending IMF and World Bank meetings in Bangkok, acknowledged the forecasts but stated the government is working towards its budget targets. Economists warn that the current economic trajectory will lead to continued weak growth and high inflation.

The IMF also forecasts a further slowdown, with growth potentially reaching 2.2% in FY2027-28, which would be even lower than during the COVID-19 pandemic. The economy is not expected to see robust recovery in the coming years, with modest growth predicted through 2030-31.

headline: 37 hours later, Chawkbazar fire fully extinguished
summary: Firefighters worked for over a day and a half to douse the blaze that broke out on Monday evening.
details: The Fire Service and Civil Defence has finally extinguished the fire at Chawkbazar after 37 hours of continuous effort.
The blaze was fully doused by 6:30 am on Wednesday, October 14, according to an official message.
Firefighters first received information about the fire around 5:00 pm on Monday.
Ten units of firefighters managed to bring the blaze under control by 5:00 am on Tuesday, but it took another 25 hours to fully extinguish it.
Kazi Nazmuzzaman, an assistant director of the Fire Service, explained that while the fire was inside, smouldering materials continued to produce smoke.
He noted that constant spraying of water was necessary to prevent the heat from smouldering materials from causing the fire to flare up again.
